title: Kinder group chats

body.heading: Mind the audience you cannot see
paragraphs: In a group chat you never quite know who is having a terrible day, reading at 2 a.m., or one message away from leaving. A little restraint with pile-ons, screenshots, and jokes at one member’s expense costs nothing and protects people you cannot see clearly.
A good test: would this message feel the same if the person it mentions were standing beside you, reading over your shoulder? In a group chat, one day they may be — chats have long memories.

body.heading: Use the side door
paragraphs: Corrections, concerns, and anything tender belong in a private message, not the square. “Loved the plan — one thought, just between us” preserves both the person and the plan. Public praise, private repair: the old rule survives every new app.
Likewise, if someone goes quiet after a joke, the kind repair happens quietly too — a small private “hope that landed okay” can undo more than you know.

body.heading: Be the warmth on purpose
paragraphs: Group chats drift toward whatever is repeated: sarcasm, alarm, or warmth. You can steer by repetition — answering the ignored message, welcoming the new member, dropping the occasional unprovoked “this group is good.” It feels small. It compounds.
Every chat has a tone-keeper, whether appointed or not. There are worse roles to volunteer for.

takeaway: Praise in the square, repair through the side door, and repeat warmth until it becomes the weather.
